title: G.S. to consider tax incentives to spur business in beach area in Gulf Shores & Orange Beach - Mullet Wrapper
content:
City will seek State Park land swap for bypass road south of Gulf Pines After several years of infrastructure projects near the city’s beachfront in surrounding neighborhoods – parking, sidewalks, streetscape, and drainage – Gulf Shores will now focus on a new direction. The city is planning a new tax incentive program to support business development in the area.
The city council met in a committee-of-the-whole session on July 6 in council chambers at City Hall to address the program.
“The Beach Walking District Area Investment Program and Waterway Village Area Investment Program are designed to support high-quality private investment that strengthens the city’s walkability, expands year-round economic activity, and elevates the city’s dining, retail, lodging, and mixed-use offerings within these priority areas,” a memo from Economic Development Coordinator Blake Phelps states. “The program provides a rebate of new taxes generated by projects, allowing investors to reduce upfront costs and improve long-term project feasibility.”
According to Phelps, the city will offer up to 50 percent tax rebates for city sales taxes, lodging taxes, and property taxes. Targeted in the program will be “high-end or destination” restaurants, boutique or specialty retail, mixed-use commercial-lodging-retail outlets, “high-end” and boutique hotels, and entertainment-focused uses.
“To be considered, interested applicants must first apply to the review committee,” Phelps’ memo states. “Potential projects will be evaluated using a transparent scoring system used in the discretion of the Review Committee.”
Among those are:
• Job creation (high-wage, year-round positions)
• Public improvements (parking, plazas, landscaping, sidewalks)
• Architectural quality
• Local ownership or local operator involvement
• Sustainability or resilience features
• Year-round operation
• Attractiveness to full- and part-time residents as well as tourists and visitors
“Higher-scoring projects may receive higher rebate percentages or longer durations,” the memo states. “Actual terms depend on project scale, public benefits, and alignment with city goals. All relevant capital investment and financing details (including proof of substantial equity, funding, or financing sources), developer experience and comparable completed projects, market studies, design schematics, engineering analyses, architectural and site plans, construction/bid cost estimates, and financial revenue projections for the city.”
Applicants whose projects are approved will then begin negotiating terms with the city on the final development agreement.
The council will also discuss an amendment to the zoning ordinance to expand the Walking Overlay District boundaries.
Also on the work session agenda:
• Consider a taxi franchise request from Granbury Executive Transport to operate a “luxury chauffeur, airport, executive, corporate, special event, and non-emergency medical transportation services.”
• Discuss a land swap with Gulf State Park to acquire land and rights of way for a bypass road south of the Gulf Pines neighborhood. East Anglian Air Ambulance is pleased to announce that G’s Fresh – one of Europe’s leading fresh produce companies – is backing its Cambridge Air Base Appeal. The family-run global fresh produce business, which is based in Barway, Ely, has pledged its support to the charity following the launch of its biggest ever fundraising appeal. East Anglian Air Ambulance is on a mission to build a new air base before the closure of Cambridge Airport in 2030. The charity has recently been granted planning permission to construct a new purpose-built facility on the outskirts of the village of Fulbourn – but needs to urgently raise £8.2 million to make it happen and is calling on local residents and businesses to come to its rescue. Without a new Cambridgeshire base, East Anglian Air Ambulance’s emergency care service will be cut in half – leaving the charity operating out of just its Norwich headquarters. This would increase tasking times to patients when they need it most – putting lives at risk. G’s Fresh, which supplies UK supermarkets with a variety of fresh produce, and which has been a supporter of East Anglian Air Ambulance for the past 25 years, has made a significant contribution to the charity’s Cambridge Air Base Appeal. Commenting, John Shropshire, Chairman of G’s Fresh, said: “The work of East Anglian Air Ambulance is a vital addition to the emergency services within East Anglia. At G’s Fresh, we operate in a mainly rural location in Cambridgeshire, with many of our colleagues living and working in remote locations that are not always easily accessible to road vehicles. Knowing that emergency aid can be onsite to any major incident very quickly is reassuring and, potentially, a lifesaver. We are pleased to be backing the Cambridge Air Base Appeal – and encourage other local businesses to get on board and do the same.” Accidents on farmland and in rural areas can be serious, and reaching someone quickly by road isn’t always straightforward. When a call comes in, East Anglian Air Ambulance's crews are ready to bring advanced treatment, care, equipment and medication straight to the scene - even in the most remote places - so help is never far away. Conor McGeown, Head of Philanthropy and Capital Appeals at East Anglian Air Ambulance, said: “We provide the very best care when the very worst happens, bringing intensive care directly to the scene of incidents in the fastest time possible. The service we offer across Cambridgeshire, Bedfordshire, Suffolk and Norfolk is only possible because of our two bases. Building a new home in Cambridgeshire is vital, ensuring we can get to people quickly. For people in cardiac arrest; for those in serious road accidents; for anyone facing a medical emergency or traumatic injury – we are a lifeline, and we are hugely grateful to the Shropshire family and everyone at G’s Fresh for their continuing support.” East Anglian Air Ambulance has made it easy for people across Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire, Norfolk and Suffolk to support the appeal: Supporters can also fundraise by hosting events or taking on challenges - from bake sales and charity balls, to marathons, skydives and other adventurous activities. Schools, businesses, sports clubs and community groups are also being encouraged to make East Anglian Air Ambulance their chosen charity and fundraise together in ways that work for them. title: Gangwon and GS sign agreement for 2.4 GW AI data center campus in Donghae - W.Media
content: Governor of the Gangwon Special Self-Governing Province, Woo Sang-ho, has signed a business agreement with Donghae City and, South Korean conglomerate, GS to establish the Donghae AI Data Center. Set to be built on a 231,000 square meter parcel of land within the Bukpyeong 2 General Industrial Complex, the AI data center is expected to be operational by 2028 on the back of a KRW 30 trillion (US$ 19.9 billion) investment GS announced in June. According to a press release issued by the Gangwon Special Self-Governing Province, the AI data center will initially have a capacity of 1.2 GW with an additional 1.2 GW expected to come online in 2029 for a total of 2.4 GW. GS will reportedly lean on its existing power infrastructure near the site of the data center which is running at 30 percent capacity due to delays in expanding transmission infrastructure. “The AI Data Center is a core infrastructure of the AI industry and a growth foundation that will drive future industrial competitiveness. The Donghae AI Data Center campus will be Gangwon’s first AI industry project and the starting point for building an AI industry ecosystem,” said Woo. “With the principle that companies focus on investment while the province takes responsibility for administration, we will provide active support at the pace companies require,” the governor added. To that end, the governor noted that the province will fast-track permits for this and other projects around the data center, while also handling the provision of essential infrastructure including water and electricity. The Donghae AI Data Center feeds South Korea’s drive to rank among the world’s top three AI powers, alongside the US and China, a push backed by a KRW 65 trillion (US$49 billion) private sector pledge toward AI development, announced in 2024 and running through 2027. As w.media covered more recently, President Lee Jae-myung announced three megaprojects for the country involving semiconductors, AI data centers, and physical AI as the country looks to grow beyond regional capital and expand into other parts of the country. The megaprojects will include involvement from Samsung Electronics, SK Group, Naver, and GS Group, among many others. By 2025, South Korea’s AI optimized data center market was worth US$ 580 million with Mordor Intelligence estimating that the market could balloon to a value of US$ 1.89 billion by 2030. However, that was before the Lee announced these megaprojects where AI data centers are expected to attract US$ 356 billion in investment alone. title: Girls head outdoors for a “digital detox” at summer camp - The Daily Reflector
content: PIEDMONT — Hundreds of girls across western and central North Carolina are gearing up to explore the outdoors at day, overnight and horse summer camp programs with Girl Scouts Carolinas Peaks to Piedmont (GSCP2P). This summer, the overnight week-long and half-week sessions of summer camp programs are hosted at Keyauwee Program Center in Sophia for girls in rising grades 2 to 12. Day camps will be hosted in Greensboro, Hickory and Black Mountain for girls in rising grades 1-5. “Girl Scout summer camp is an amazing opportunity for all girls to explore new possibilities outside of their normal routines,” said Elaine Loyack, Chief Executive Officer at GSCP2P. “At camp, girls can grow their independence and confidence through hands-on learning and make new friends that lift them up in a safe, supportive space.” This year’s theme, Explore More Camp, encourages campers to engage in a variety of activities during their experience and “explore more” than what they normally would do. Programs are full of favorite traditional camp activities like swimming, archery, boating and campfires plus an opportunity to choose from a variety of new sessions like visiting the barn, participating in sports and games, learning new crafting skills and more. This year, all overnight campers will get to enjoy an equestrian experience on site at the Circle C Equestrian Center at no additional cost. Camp is for all girls and Girl Scouts, so they do not have to be a current member to have an exciting summer camp adventure. The GSCP2P council also offers financial assistance so more girls can attend summer camp. After registering for a program and paying the $50 non-refundable deposit, families can access the online financial aid application. In 2025, overnight campers who applied for financial assistance received an average of $280 to use on registration fees. There is still time to reserve a spot to Explore More Camp for a full week or half week session of overnight camp and day camps. Registrations should be complete at least 10 days before the session start date. Visit www.CampLikeAGirl.org to view the 2026 Summer Camp Program Guide and discover all the outdoor summer fun with Girl Scouts. Girl Scouts Carolinas Peaks to Piedmont, a United Way agency, is one of 111 councils nationwide chartered by Girl Scouts of the USA to deliver Girl Scout programs within specific geographic boundaries. The local council serves over 5,600 girls and 4,400 adult volunteers in 40 counties and maintains three camp properties and four service centers offering unique experiences for girls and adults. For more information on how to join, volunteer, reconnect or donate to GSCP2P, call 800-672-2148 or visit www.girlscoutsp2p.org. We Are Girl Scouts: Girl Scouts bring their dreams to life and work together to build a better world. Through programs from coast to coast, Girl Scouts of all backgrounds and abilities can be unapologetically themselves as they discover  their strengths and rise to meet new challenges—whether they want to climb to the top of a tree or the top of their class, lace up their boots for a hike or advocate for climate justice or make their first best friends. Backed by trusted adult volunteers, mentors and millions of alums, Girl Scouts lead the way as they find their voices and make changes that affect the issues most important to them. title: ASUS ROG Strix GS-BE18000 [Review] – Wi-Fi 7 That Slaps. - G Style Magazine
content: Over the past several weeks, the ASUS ROG Strix GS-BE18000 has become the centerpiece of my home network, handling everything from competitive multiplayer gaming and nightly livestreams to downloading massive game updates and remote gaming sessions throughout my apartment. My home presents a unique challenge. I live in a pre-war New York City apartment building with thick brick walls that have always been the enemy of strong Wi-Fi coverage. Even high-end routers I’ve tested over the years have struggled to consistently maintain peak speeds from room to room.Wireless Routers The GS-BE18000, however, brought something genuinely new to the table. Between its Wi-Fi 7 capabilities, Automated Frequency Coordination (AFC), and seamless integration with my existing ASUS ZenWiFi XT9 through AiMesh, it delivered one of the most consistently reliable wireless experiences I’ve had in years. Unlike many gaming routers that resemble futuristic spacecraft covered in antennas, the GS-BE18000 takes a far more refined approach. The compact vertical chassis looks clean enough to blend into a living room while still maintaining the unmistakable ROG aesthetic. The internal antenna design keeps the exterior tidy without sacrificing wireless performance, and the subtle Aura RGB lighting gives it just enough personality without becoming distracting.Computer & Video Games Build quality is excellent throughout, and despite its smaller footprint, the router feels substantial and well-built. Around the back you’ll find one of its biggest strengths: eight 2.5GbE Ethernet ports, including two dedicated Gaming Ports. These ports automatically prioritize traffic for connected gaming devices, making them especially useful for console players or anyone who wants optimized gaming performance without diving into advanced networking settings. The GS-BE18000 is a tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router capable of delivering up to 18Gbps of combined theoretical wireless throughput across the 2.4GHz, 5GHz, and 6GHz bands. ASUS pairs that with a quad-core 2.0GHz processor, 2GB of DDR4 memory, and support for the latest Wi-Fi 7 technologies, including 320MHz channels, Multi-Link Operation (MLO), 4K-QAM, OFDMA, MU-MIMO, WPA3 security, and Multi-RU Puncturing.Computers & Electronics One of the router’s defining features is Automated Frequency Coordination (AFC). Once enabled, AFC allows the 6GHz radio to operate at Standard Power in supported regions, significantly extending usable 6GHz coverage compared to traditional Low Power Indoor operation. Instead of simply chasing higher benchmark numbers, AFC improves real-world performance by allowing devices to maintain stronger connections farther away from the router. ASUS also continues to offer one of the strongest software ecosystems available in consumer networking. ASUSWRT 4.0 provides an intuitive interface packed with advanced networking tools while remaining approachable for less experienced users. Setup can be completed entirely through a web browser without requiring an online account, or through the ASUS Router app on both iOS and Android.Computer & Video Games Another standout feature is Smart Home Master, which allows users to quickly create dedicated wireless networks for gaming, smart home devices, VPN traffic, family devices, or guest access. Having the ability to organize different types of devices into their own SSIDs is a thoughtful addition that helps simplify network management without adding unnecessary complexity. One feature I found particularly compelling is USB WAN. By connecting an iPhone or Android smartphone directly to the USB port, the GS-BE18000 can instantly use a cellular connection as a backup internet source whenever your primary ISP goes offline. Anyone who has experienced an unexpected internet outage while working remotely or streaming understands how valuable this feature can be. The setup process is straightforward and requires no additional hardware or subscription.Wireless Routers The GS-BE18000 has been powering my streaming setup every night while simultaneously handling downloads, smart home devices, video uploads, and competitive gaming sessions without missing a beat. My desktop remains connected through one of the dedicated 2.5GbE gaming ports for maximum stability, while much of my wireless testing focused on the ROG Ally X. Pairing the router with the ROG Ally X also unlocked ASUS’ Game First integration. The handheld automatically recognized the ROG router and prioritized its network traffic with virtually no configuration required. It’s a small quality-of-life feature, but one that highlights how well ASUS’ gaming ecosystem works together. The biggest surprise during my testing was AFC. Living in a pre-war New York City apartment with thick brick walls has always presented challenges for wireless networking. Areas that traditionally forced devices onto weaker connections maintained impressive throughput, even several rooms away from the router. ASUS rates the GS-BE18000 for homes up to approximately 3,300 square feet, and based on my experience, that estimate feels realistic depending on your home’s layout and construction.Computers & Electronics I also integrated my existing ASUS ZenWiFi XT9 into the network through AiMesh, extending coverage into the far end of my apartment where I often spend time gaming on the ROG Ally X. The experience felt seamless, making it seem as though the wireless access point was always in the same room with me. For larger homes or more challenging layouts, AiMesh remains one of ASUS’ biggest strengths, supporting more than forty compatible Wi-Fi 6, Wi-Fi 6E, and Wi-Fi 7 routers and mesh systems. Users also have the flexibility to deploy wired or wireless backhaul and manually choose which band AiMesh uses for node communication. It’s worth mentioning that wireless mesh systems naturally introduce some backhaul overhead when using wireless connections between nodes. If your home doesn’t require mesh, operating the GS-BE18000 as a standalone router allows all available wireless resources to focus entirely on connected client devices. For homes that do need additional coverage, however, the convenience and stability of AiMesh easily outweigh that tradeoff.Computer & Video Games While Wi-Fi 7 devices naturally benefit the most from the router’s newest technologies, you don’t need an entirely Wi-Fi 7 household to appreciate what the GS-BE18000 offers. Wi-Fi 6E devices immediately benefit from expanded access to the 6GHz band, while Wi-Fi 5 and Wi-Fi 6 devices still take advantage of ASUS’ improved radios, antenna design, gaming prioritization, and extensive software features. Even internet connections well below multi-gigabit speeds can benefit from stronger throughput and better signal quality at moderate and long distances throughout the home. If there’s one thing I’d like to expand upon in future testing, it would be standardized LAN throughput benchmarking alongside my real-world testing. While my experience throughout weeks of streaming and gaming demonstrated excellent stability, pairing those impressions with measurable LAN speed testing would provide an additional point of comparison for readers looking at raw network performance.Computers & Electronics The ASUS ROG Strix GS-BE18000 is one of the easiest gaming routers I’ve recommended in recent years. Rather than focusing solely on headline speeds, ASUS built a router that improves the overall networking experience through thoughtful hardware, practical software, and genuinely useful features. AFC significantly improves the usefulness of 6GHz networking, AiMesh continues to be one of the best mesh ecosystems available, USB WAN provides valuable peace of mind during ISP outages, and Smart Home Master makes managing a modern connected home remarkably simple. Add in eight 2.5GbE ports, dedicated Gaming Ports, Game First integration for ASUS gaming hardware, and one of the most comprehensive router interfaces on the market, and the GS-BE18000 becomes much more than another Wi-Fi 7 router.Computer & Video Games ASUS also backs the GS-BE18000 with a three-year limited warranty, continuing one of the strongest warranty programs available in the consumer networking space. For more on GS-BE18000 and gaming, follow my socials here – I also stream Mon-Sat @9pm ET over on Twitch, TikTok, and YouTube

title: Championship Battles, Canadians in Spotlight at CTMP - Sportscar365
content: Less Than 100 points cover top four in GS; 11 Canadians split three GS, eight TCR entries… A challenging end to an otherwise clean IMSA Michelin Pilot Challenge race at Watkins Glen International has set the stage for the second half of the season, where it’s anyone’s guess who will emerge at the head of the championship battles leaving Canadian Tire Motorsport Park. There are 42 cars, split 29 GS and 13 TCR, for Round 6 of the season, which sees the top four in GS are now covered by just 80 points, which includes entries from four different teams and manufacturers. Turner Motorsport’s No. 95 BMW M4 GT4 EVO of Luca Mars and Dillon Machavern still leads by 60 points, with their 17th place finish at Watkins Glen not at all reflective of what looked to be their fifth top-five finish in as many races. Debris caused a puncture to the car in the final moments of the race. Just 20 points cover second through fourth. Two-time winners Ibiza Farm Motorsport sit second with Michael Cooper and Moisey Uretsky in their No. 44 McLaren Artura GT4, ten ahead of third-placed Bryce Ward in his No. 57 Winward Racing Mercedes-AMG GT4 and ten more ahead of fourth-placed Nate Cicero and Robert Noaker in their No. 13 McCumbee McAleer Racing Ford Mustang GT4. Lurking in fifth is Austin Krainz and Stevan McAleer in their No. 27 Auto Technic Racing BMW M4 GT4 EVO. Despite an 11th-place result at Watkins Glen, they’re only 140 back, and heading to two venues where the No. 27 car podiumed in 2025 at CTMP and Road America, respectively. In TCR, three Bryan Herta Autosport Hyundai Elantra N TCRs maintain the top three positions in points, owing in large part to consistency. Four podiums from Bryson Morris and Mason Filippi see their No. 33 Hyundai at the head of the field by 80 points over teammates Preston Brown and Belgian driver Denis Dupont, who resides in Montreal, in their No. 76 Hyundai, with Mark Wilkins and Madison Aust third in their No. 98 Hyundai 140 back. The team’s No. 18 Hyundai (Harry Gottsacker, Lance Bergstein) sits fifth in points. Wilkins is one of three active Canadian drivers to win a Pilot Challenge race at CTMP, along with last year’s winners Karl Wittmer and LP Montour in their No. 93 MMG Honda Civic FL5 TCR. Unfortunately for the all-Canadian Honda entry, early race mechanical woes at the LP Building Solutions 120 left Wittmer and Montour falling down the standings to sixth, 250 points in arrears after winning the previous round at the Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course. The 29 GS cars feature three Canadian drivers, including brothers Travis and Trevor Hill in the No. 22 Shopify Racing Porsche 718 GT4 RS Clubsport, Samantha Tan in her No. 38 ST Racing by Random Vandals BMW. The Canadians are more prevalent among the 13 TCR cars. Beyond the already mentioned Wilkins, Wittmer and Montour, Baker Racing has a quartet of Canadians in the father-and-son duo of Dean and Sam Baker, James Vance  and Kenny Riedmann split between their Nos. 52 and 56 Audi RS 3 LMS TCRs. The CTMP 120 takes the green flag Saturday at 1:25 p.m. EST with live streaming coverage on Peacock and ad-free courtesy of Michelin on IMSA’s Official YouTube channel. title: Mr. G’s Pizzeria marks 30 years as friendship preserves legacy | Bryan - College Station - Community Impact
content: As Mr. G’s Pizzeria celebrates three decades in downtown Bryan, owner Susan Carnes reflects on the unlikely friendship preserving the restaurant’s legacy and inspiring its next chapter. For years, customers walking into Mr. G’s Pizzeria in Historic Downtown Bryan were likely to find founder Giovanni “Mr. G” Cerone sitting at a dining room table, paperwork spread out before him as he greeted regulars, welcomed newcomers and shared stories from a life that had taken him from Italy to Texas. Nearly five years after Mr. G's passing, that presence still lingers inside the 30-year-old restaurant. His recipes remain, as do many of the traditions which made the pizzeria a downtown Bryan institution. Now, as the restaurant celebrates its 30th anniversary, the family he chose is carrying his legacy into the business’s next chapter. Mr. G’s Pizzeria will celebrate 30 years in business this month while expanding its footprint with the opening of g’s Southside Italian Cafe in College Station. The new café, expected to open with a soft launch in mid-July before a grand opening this fall, isn’t replacing the downtown restaurant. Instead, owner Susan Carnes described it as “a nod and a tribute” to Mr. G. Carnes wasn’t looking to own a restaurant when she first met Mr. G. She and her husband had just celebrated their 10-year anniversary at Downtown Uncorked, which was located in downtown Bryan until it moved to south College Station in 2021. The couple stopped into Mr. G’s to grab a pizza for their children at home. Instead, Carnes found herself talking with the restaurant’s owner for nearly two hours. “It was like love at first sight, friendship at first sight,” she said with a laugh. “These two families just adopted each other.” “He says–in his little Italian accent–he goes, ‘Susan, if you [don’t] take it, [I’ll] close at the end of the month,’” she recalled him saying. Although she had little restaurant experience beyond waiting tables in college, Carnes and her family stepped in during the uncertainty of the COVID-19 pandemic. Today, her children have grown up inside the business much like several employees who have spent decades there. One longtime pizza cook has worked at Mr. G’s since she was 15 years old, and Carnes’ teenage son will soon bus tables at the new café. Mr. G’s widow Houda remains closely involved and has even shared recipes from her former College Station restaurant, Cenare, for the new concept. Much has changed since Mr. G’s opened in 1996, but the recipes that built its reputation remain largely untouched. The restaurant continues to serve its signature pizzas from classic Margherita and Hawaiian pies to house specialties like the Lu Pizza, which is topped with mozzarella, feta, caramelized onions and prosciutto. The menu also includes calzones, pasta, subs, salads, garlic bread, gluten-free and keto options and desserts like tiramisu and cannoli. At the heart of it all is the pizza dough recipe Mr. G. brought to Bryan decades ago. Today, Carnes said only two people know how to make it. While the downtown pizzeria will continue serving its signature and longtime favorites, the new café will expand on the family’s Italian roots. The kitchen at the College Station location will also become the primary location for preparing dough, sauces and other ingredients used by both restaurants. Despite the expansion, Carnes said Bryan remains home. She calls the downtown restaurant a “7,000 square-foot elephant” that has survived recessions, COVID-19 and decades of changing restaurant trends. “It would leave a hole in the heart,” she said. “So, as long as we’re able, Mr. G’s downtown Bryan will be [here].” The restaurant continues to draw crowds during First Friday events, hosts live entertainment and private events and remains one of downtown Bryan’s long-running eateries. For Carnes, opening another restaurant isn’t about growing a brand nearly as much as preserving a friendship. The lowercase “g” in g’s Southside Italian Cafe was intentional, she said, as it’s not meant to replace or compete with Mr. G’s. Carnes told Community Impact Mr G’s plans to have specials and parties to celebrate 30 years. In the meantime, Mr. G’s will operate during normal business hours, staying open until 9 p.m. during the week and 10 p.m. on Fridays and Saturdays. title: Shaped by Champions: Logitech G's PRO X SUPERLIGHT 2 DEX Gaming Mouse - Global Design News
content:
PRO X SUPERLIGHT 2 DEX Wireless Gaming Mouse was designed in collaboration with the world’s elite esports athletes. It embodies Logitech G’s product design methodology to meet the performance needs of those competing at the highest level. To create a high-performance mouse for the global esports community, we started with a proven favourite: Logitech G PRO X Superlight Wireless Gaming Mouse. Designers stripped it to its skeleton and sculpted a new, more supportive shape on the high-performance chassis of its predecessor. Logitech G PRO X Superlight 2 DEX Lightspeed Wireless Gaming Mouse by Logitech G, won a 2025 Good Design Award from The Chicago Athenaeum: Museum of Architecture and Design and European Centre for Architecture, Art, Design, and Urban Studies. After years of iteration and global collaboration, we landed on a shape that feels “invisible” in the hand, allowing players’ true skill to shine through. Dozens of CNC and 3D-printed prototypes were tested to fine-tune every curve and contour. We went the extra mile by working with the world’s top competitive esports players. As the leading provider of pro-level gear, we know that with the right gaming gear, players can achieve their goals, break records, and build careers. This is Design by Collaboration, a distinctive approach that merges insights from initial concept to final production. We worked directly with pro teams across the globe to gather actionable insights on grip preferences, in-game movements, and performance goals. By sitting down with players, we got as many hands on the mouse as possible, assessing how it fit diverse grip styles, testing materials, and dialing in every detail. We had pros define what matters most, and DEX was designed to reflect their expertise and preferences. The main objectives: increased comfort, hand placement freedom, and a pro-grade wireless gaming mouse that empowers peak performance. It was critical to look and feel comfortable, and when held, should instantly make players feel like they could play for as long as desired without discomfort. Our designers and engineers used this feedback to innovate, refine, and deliver a mouse that feels less like hardware and more like a true extension of one’s hand, a tool designed to help pros perform their best, every time. We worked closely with our ergonomics team to ensure DEX achieves the sensation of a mouse working like a true extension of the hand. No two gamers are alike, so its shape had to support a variety of grips and play styles. DEX’s height was increased asymmetrically for more mid-hand support, with curves towards the back to fit players’ backhands. This ergo shape reduces fatigue and improves natural control during high-stakes tournaments. This shape is essential in pro esports matches, as it empowers players to boost accuracy and control in games where precision is everything. DEX’s design plays a critical role in enabling space for technological innovation. By optimising internal architecture by streamlining the layout, minimising unnecessary materials, and refining the shell structure, designers created more room for advanced technologies like higher-capacity sensors, custom-tuned switches, and wireless communication modules. A thoughtfully engineered form improves airflow and thermal management, which is essential as processing power and polling rates increase. DEX is packed with innovations tailored to unique needs of pro players. Its HERO 2 sensor delivers pinpoint tracking at over 44,000 dots per inch at up to 88G-forces of acceleration, at speeds of up to 888 inches per second. The HERO 2 sensor was engineered to exceed human capabilities with ultimate precision and redefine what’s possible in competitive gaming. With HERO 2, DEX ensures perfect accuracy during lightning-fast movements, a crucial advantage when a single pixel can be the difference between a win and a loss. 888 IPS is an incredible achievement technologically and as a speed metric. 888 IPS equates moving your mouse at 80 km/h, 20% faster than the closest competitor. DEX’s HERO 2 sensor achieved the highest speed on the market to perform well above the needs of our pro players. To match this, our engineers upgraded our LIGHTSPEED wireless technology to support 8 kHz polling, offering a faster, more responsive connection and ultra-low latency that beats wired mice every time. Hybrid LIGHTFORCE switches combine the speed of an optical sensor with the satisfying click of a mechanical switch, so every action feels fast, crisp, and reliable. Weighing in at just 60g, the weight of a few US nickels, and delivering up to 95 hours of battery life, DEX is designed to keep up game after game, allowing players to trust their mouse and stay focused on what matters most: securing victories and achieving their professional goals. title: GS Group Builds Asia's Largest AI Data Center in Donghae - 조선일보
content: 120-trillion-won project in Donghae to reach 2.4GW by 2029, positioning Gangwon as AI hub GS Group is building Asia’s largest AI data center in Donghae, Gangwon Province. It is a mega-project with a maximum investment of 120 trillion Korean won, to be developed to a scale of 2.4GW by 2029. Amid a global surge in demand for data centers due to AI expansion, Gangwon Province has moved to establish itself as a hub for AI infrastructure. Gangwon Province, Donghae City, and GS Group signed a business agreement on the 6th at a small meeting room in the Gangwon Provincial Government Office to establish the ‘Donghae AI Data Center Campus.’ Those attending the agreement ceremony included Gangwon Governor Woo Sang-ho, Donghae Mayor Lee Jeong-hak, GS Vice Chairman Hong Soon-gi, and GS E&R Representative Hwang Byeong-so. The Donghae AI Data Center will be built on approximately 70,000 pyeong of land within the Bukpyeong Second General Industrial Complex in Donghae City. The plan is to first construct 1.2GW by 2028, then add another 1.2GW by 2029 to complete a total scale of 2.4GW. As a single AI data center, it will be the largest in Asia. GS announced the plan to build the Donghae AI Data Center at the ‘National Report Meeting on the Three Mega Projects for Korea’s Great Leap Forward’ on the 29th of last month. The total investment cost is 30 trillion Korean won, and including costs for graphics processing units (GPUs) and memory, it is expected to reach up to 120 trillion Korean won. The project site, the Bukpyeong Second General Industrial Complex, is an industrial complex that GS began construction on in 2016 and completed in 2022. With the site already secured and power supply conditions in place, the project is expected to proceed swiftly. Measures to secure power and water, the core elements of an AI data center, have also been prepared. The 1.2GW-scale facility to be built by 2028 will receive power linked to GS Donghae Power’s power generation facilities. The cooling system will operate using an immersion cooling method, where servers are submerged in special cooling oil, and approximately 1,100 tons of industrial water per day. Gangwon Province plans to operate a fast-track system for permits and licenses to allow companies to focus on investment, and actively support infrastructure such as power and water supply. Governor Woo’s first official order upon taking office on the 1st to form the ‘AI Data Center Promotion Team’ was also aimed at accelerating the project. This agreement is significant as it marks the realization of Governor Woo’s vision for fostering the AI industry, which he revealed in an interview with this newspaper last week. At the time, Governor Woo disclosed that alongside GS’s 2.4GW project in Donghae, SK Group is also pushing to build a 1GW-scale AI data center in the Gangwon region. If SK’s project proceeds, Gangwon Province could become the country’s largest AI infrastructure cluster with a total of 3.4GW-scale AI data centers. Globally, competition to secure AI data centers is intensifying. McKinsey & Company, a global consulting firm, projected that while demand for AI data centers will grow by 19–22% annually, supply will lag, leading to a shortage of approximately 15GW in the U.S. alone by 2030. Consequently, global companies are expanding AI infrastructure investments to regions outside the U.S. Gangwon Province highlights its strengths: abundant power supply, vast industrial land, and relatively fewer location restrictions. AI data centers are power-intensive industries that consume far more electricity than general data centers, giving regions capable of large-scale power supply a competitive edge. The capital region faces difficulties in adding large-scale AI data centers due to saturated power grids. Gangwon Governor Woo Sang-ho stated, “AI data centers are the core infrastructure of the AI industry and the growth foundation that will determine future industrial competitiveness. The Donghae AI Data Center will be the starting point for building Gangwon’s AI industry ecosystem and a key hub for enhancing South Korea’s AI industry competitiveness.”

title: South Korean prosecutors indict four major refiners over allegations of oil price collusion - CNBC
content:
South Korean prosecutors on Monday indicted four major domestic oil refiners for violating fair trade laws, alleging they colluded to drive up domestic fuel prices following the Middle East conflict. HD Hyundai Oilbank, SK Energy, GS Caltex, and S-Oil were the four companies that breached the nation’s fair trade act, according to Yonhap News Agency. HD Hyundai Oilbank and SK Energy colluded on 14.2 trillion won ($9.2 billion) worth of oil sales, Yonhap reported, citing prosecutors. Factoring in GS Caltex and S-Oil, which allegedly mimicked those prices, the total anticompetitive impact stands at roughly 26 trillion won, the report said. The investigation was initiated after domestic oil prices sharply rose following the U.S.–Iran conflict, prosecutors said, finding that collusion by pricing executives at two of the firms over the timing and scale of the hikes was the primary driver. The prosecution said the collusion was not a standalone incident but a long-standing, systemic practice that surfaced during a time of global crisis. In March, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung warned on X that oil refiners and corporations engaged in price-fixing would be held accountable, vowing to deploy all lawful measures against unethical business practices. Shares of the oil refiners and their owners were still higher. S-Oil gained 6.08%, SK Innovation, a parent company for SK Energy, advanced 1.58% while HD Hyundai rose 1.21% and GS Holdings, which jointly controls refiner GS Caltex with Chevron through its energy unit, rose 6.99%.
